vocabulary.meaning_en: the strength and power to be active
vocabulary.example: The children have so much energy in the morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a pleasant quality that makes people like you
vocabulary.example: Her charm made everyone feel welcome.

vocabulary.meaning_en: attractive in an exciting and stylish way
vocabulary.example: The actress wore a glamorous dress at the ceremony.
The new manager brought vitality to the team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: full of energy, life or bright colour
vocabulary.example: The market is full of vibrant colours.
The view from the mountain was amazing.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a bad mood and easily annoyed
vocabulary.example: My brother is always grumpy before breakfast.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to complain in an annoying way
vocabulary.example: He moans about the weather every day.
I was annoyed because the bus was late.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the power to change what people think or do
vocabulary.example: Teachers have a big influence on children.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who follows someone's account on social media
vocabulary.example: She has thousands of followers online.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the feeling or mood of a place
vocabulary.example: The café has a calm atmosphere.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way you feel at a particular time
vocabulary.example: I'm in a good mood today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: relaxed; used with friends, not in official situations
something nice you say about someone

vocabulary.note_en: Don't confuse it with 'complement' (something that completes). They sound the same.

fine_lines.title: fire vs lit vs slay
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الكلمات الثلاث عاميّة وتعني «رائع جداً». fire و lit صفتان تأتيان بعد is: It's fire / It's lit. أما slay ففعل: He slays / She slayed، ويُستعمل غالباً للإعجاب بمظهر شخص أو أدائه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: All three are slang for 'amazing'. 'Fire' and 'lit' are adjectives used after 'is': It's fire. It's lit. 'Slay' is a verb: She slays. He slayed. It is often used about how someone looks or performs.

fine_lines.title: oomph vs pizzazz
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما عن الطاقة والجاذبية. oomph تركّز على القوة والحماس والطاقة في الأداء. pizzazz تركّز على البريق والأناقة واللمعان (شخص أو تصميم أو لون لافت).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both describe exciting energy. 'Oomph' is about power and enthusiasm. 'Pizzazz' is about glamour, style and sparkle.

examples.sentence: The speaker had real oomph – nobody felt bored.
The red lights gave the shop window real pizzazz.

fine_lines.title: mardy vs miffed
fine_lines.explanation_ar: mardy صفة لشخص متجهّم يتذمّر وينزعج بسهولة (كلمة بريطانية من شمال إنجلترا). miffed تعني منزعجاً قليلاً بسبب شيء محدد فعله أحدهم: miffed about something.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Mardy' describes a person who is grumpy, moans and gets annoyed easily (British, from the north of England). 'Miffed' means a little annoyed because of something specific: miffed about something.

examples.sentence: Don't be so mardy – it's only a short walk.
She was miffed that nobody thanked her.

expressions.meaning_ar: حماس وطاقة وجاذبية تجعل الشخص أو الشيء ممتعاً ومؤثراً
expressions.example: Our team needs a bit more oomph in the second half.

expressions.meaning_en: an attractive mix of style, glamour and energy
expressions.example: The new logo has real pizzazz.
Have you tried this new game? It's fire!

expressions.meaning_en: grumpy, moaning and easily annoyed (British, informal)
expressions.example: He gets mardy when he's hungry.

expressions.meaning_ar: نفوذ أو شهرة، خصوصاً على وسائل التواصل؛ وكفعل: يضرب
expressions.meaning_en: influence or fame, especially on social media; as a verb it can mean 'to hit'
expressions.example: She has a lot of clout online, so brands want to work with her.

expressions.meaning_ar: الجوّ أو الإحساس الذي يعطيه مكان أو شخص
expressions.meaning_en: the mood or feeling you get from a place or person
expressions.example: This library has a really calm vibe.

expressions.meaning_ar: طلب معرفة الجوّ أو المزاج العام
expressions.meaning_en: checking the mood of a person or place
expressions.example: Vibe check: is everyone happy with the plan?
I was a bit miffed when they started without me.

expressions.meaning_ar: يرسل رسالة أو بريداً إلكترونياً سريعاً
expressions.meaning_en: informal: to send someone an email or text message
expressions.example: I'll ping you the address later.

expressions.meaning_en: slang: to be amazing or impressive; the old meaning is 'to kill'
expressions.example: She slayed at the science fair – everyone loved her project.

grammar.title: Slang words as adjectives and verbs
grammar.explanation_ar: بعض الكلمات العامّية تتصرف كصفة فتأتي بعد فعل be: It's fire / It was lit / He's mardy / I'm miffed. وبعضها فعل يُصرَّف عادياً: slay → slayed، ping → pinged. وبعضها اسم يأتي بعد have أو a: She has clout / It has a good vibe / He has oomph.
grammar.explanation_en: Some slang words work as adjectives after 'be': It's fire. It was lit. He's mardy. Some are verbs and change form: slay → slayed, ping → pinged. Some are nouns after 'have' or 'a': She has clout. It has a good vibe.
examples: I'll ping you tomorrow. / She pinged me yesterday.
This room has a nice vibe.
